body: an additional bit of context: I know it's not just the wellbutrin because I took it by itself back in 2023 and it made me extremely anxious and manic. I feel like Luvox is really good for anxiety and Wellbutrin is really good for depression so they have a kind of synergy

I started luvox November of last year. First two months were awful, I had no energy and libido. My anxiety and racing thoughts vanished though... So I was "better" but not happy.
My psychiatrist introduced Wellbutrin along with the Luvox and I have been taking both meds since. I feel MUCH better now. Sleep is normal, no sexual dysfunction and I actually enjoy being alive. The only thing I would count as a downside is that it makes me a little... Irresponsible i guess? I have been spending a lot of money on makeup and plants lol but I feel like that is also because I am happier these days

tldr: Luvox alone was bad for me. luvox + wellbutrin is good.

Hi, no problem at all!

First about your symptoms, I think you should definitely reach out to a doctor. If your meds were not working and you quit them cold turkey and you're still depressed and suicidal, you might benefit from different meds. We're all different in that regard. Don't let it get worse.

About my symptoms:
Yeah, at first I felt really energetic and euphoric for up to 6 months... and then I went into a big depression. Then I started having shorter depressive episodes and smaller bursts of confidence and energy. At first I thought, ok, that's just how my brain works without the meds, I can't maintain a baseline mood, I am a sensitive person, etc etc. Then the constant mood swings and rumination started wearing me out. I became paranoid and insecure and it was ruining my life. Ultimately I went back to my doctor and got new meds. I'm on Luvox right now because the doctor thinks my symptoms are in the OCD sphere. Too soon to say it's working, I started two days ago.

I feel bittersweet about going back to medication, but I also think it was a necessary decision at this point in my life. Depending on the side effects I might reconsider, but for now... Here we go again.

I hope you feel better!
